summary: Owned units s0023–s0044 contain no births, deaths, or ages. The sealed narrative dates Yin Hao’s first letter as 揚州刺史 before Wang Xizhi accepted 護軍, then a later 時殷浩與桓溫不協 cluster that ends in 浩遂行果為姚襄所敗. Jinshu 穆帝紀 (Emperor Mu of Eastern Jin, 永和) dates Yin Hao’s Yang appointment to 永和二年三月 (conventional AD 346), Huan Wen’s Jingzhou command to 永和元年八月 (345), Yin Hao’s first northern march to 永和八年九月 (352), Yao Xiang’s revolt and the Shan Sang rout to 永和九年冬十月 (353; proleptic Gregorian 永和九年 runs 353-02-20 to 354-02-08, so the tenth month remains AD 353), and Yin Hao’s dismissal to 永和十年二月 (354). Claim-153’s 351–353 window is Wang Xizhi’s own Kuaiji-period letters around that campaign and is supported. Claim-155 dates Wang Dao’s own recruitment attempt to 王丞相時, bounded by Eastern Jin preeminence and his 咸康五年 death (339), and is supported. Claim-173 and hints-p018 correctly give Yao Xiang’s own rout of Yin Hao as AD 353. Four clusters fail. Claim-169 and hints-p014 stamp Yin Hao’s 揚州刺史 attestation with Wang’s 351–353 Kuaiji slice, which is neither the 346 appointment nor the 346–354 tenure. Claim-170 and hints-p015 treat 尚子平之志 as Shang Ziping’s Guangwu-era life; the Chinese is Wang Xizhi’s later model-citation (retrospective), and AD 25–57 is a reign-span, not an event window (Hou Hanshu only has 建武中 for the wander story). Claim-171 converts 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東 to 189–194, but Hou Hanshu 獻帝紀 (Emperor Xian, 初平/興平) dates that mission to 初平三年八月 (192); 189 is the political start of 漢末, not this embassy, and hints-p016’s 192–194 still uses the 194 death as an activity end and contradicts the claim. Claim-172 and hints-p017 start Huan Wen’s 不協 at the 345 Jingzhou appointment, a different event; 殷浩傳 places the mutual suspicion after the Shu conquest, and this chapter’s 時 is the later Kuaiji/北伐 moment.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi wrote to Yin Hao during the Hao–Wen rift and the northern campaign after becoming Kuaiji neishi.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Wang Xizhi, not Yin Hao or Huan Wen. After 羲之既拜護軍…會稽內史, the chapter’s 時殷浩與桓溫不協, 及浩將北伐, and 浩遂行果為姚襄所敗 are his own admonitory letters and the campaign he tried to stop. 穆帝紀 dates the Shan Sang rout to 永和九年冬十月 under Emperor Mu’s 永和 reign; a proleptic Gregorian table for that regnal year runs 353-02-20 to 354-02-08, so the tenth month stays AD 353 (Academia Sinica’s pre-1582 Julian default would not move the Western year). The same biography’s 永和九年蘭亭 gathering independently places him in Kuaiji that spring. The 351 start is the conventional 會稽 appointment reconstructed from 王述’s mourning and the 永和十年 note that 王述 was 前會稽內史; together 351–353 is uncertainty about this letter cluster, not activity across a dynasty.

evidence.quote: 羲之既拜護軍，又苦求宣城郡，不許，乃以為右軍將軍、會稽內史。
及浩將北伐，羲之以為必敗，以書止之

itemChecks.event: Wang Dao tried to bring Wang Xizhi into the administration while serving as chancellor.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Wang Dao. 直王丞相時果欲內吾 is Wang Xizhi recalling Dao’s own attempt to take him into office, not a later commemoration. The letter gives no year, so the interval must be uncertainty about that attempt during Dao’s Eastern Jin preeminence. 建武/太興 founding of the Jiankang court supplies the 317 start; 晉書成帝紀 records 咸康五年秋七月庚申…王導薨, conventionally AD 339, as the latest possible year. Formal 丞相 begins only in 咸康四年, but 王丞相 is the ordinary name for Dao’s chancellorship, and 317–339 describes when the undated recruitment could fall rather than claiming he recruited every year.

evidence.quote: 直王丞相時果欲內吾，誓不許之，手跡猶存，由來尚矣

itemChecks.event: Yin Hao, as Inspector of Yang, urged Wang Xizhi to accept office and later ignored warnings before the northern campaign.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Yin Hao. 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之 is his own inspectorate letter, written before Wang accepted 護軍 (s0034). 穆帝紀, Emperor Mu, 永和二年三月丙子，以前司徒左長史殷浩爲建武將軍、揚州刺史; 殷浩傳 adds 自三月至七月，乃受拜焉 (conventional AD 346). He is still 揚州刺史 when degraded 永和十年二月 (354). The 351–353 interval copies Wang Xizhi’s Kuaiji/campaign slice and is not the title’s tenure, not the s0024 letter’s earliest possible date, and not a mere uncertainty band around one event. The later 不協/北伐 cluster is 永和八–九年 (352–353). explicit-event-contextual-date overstates a borrowed window.

evidence.quote: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之，勸使應命
羲之既拜護軍，又苦求宣城郡，不許，乃以為右軍將軍、會稽內史。

itemChecks.event: The chapter cites Shang Ziping only as Wang Xizhi's model for leaving public life, not Shang's own dated act.
itemChecks.reason: The Chinese 便懷尚子平之志 is Wang Xizhi, in an Eastern Jin letter, invoking a famous hermit’s resolve. That is later reception, not Shang Ziping’s own event, and must not feed a life interval or active hint. AD 25–57 is Emperor Guangwu’s whole reign used as if Shang were active throughout it; even the external wander story in 後漢書逸民傳 is only 建武中, not a reign-length window. Keep the mention; do not date it as living activity.

evidence.quote: 自兒娶女嫁，便懷尚子平之志，數與親知言之，非一日也。

itemChecks.event: Ma Midi was sent as Grand Tutor to console the east of the passes at the end of the Han.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Ma Midi; a later-written letter may still attest his own embassy. The source phrase is 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東, i.e. that mission, not his entire late-Han career. 後漢書獻帝紀, Emperor Xian, 初平三年秋七月庚子…馬日磾為太傅…八月，遣日磾及太僕趙歧，持節慰撫天下. 初平三年 is AD 192 (初平 = 190–193). 189 is 中平六年/初平元年, when he was not yet 太傅 and was not this envoy. 194 is 興平元年, when 太傅馬日磾薨於壽春, a death not stated here. 189–194 therefore invents both ends and is not an explicit conversion of 漢末.

evidence.quote: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東

itemChecks.event: Huan Wen was at odds with Yin Hao while Wang Xizhi tried to restore inner-outer peace.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Huan Wen’s own rift with Yin Hao (時殷浩與桓溫不協), not his 345 Jingzhou appointment. 穆帝紀, 永和元年八月…以…桓溫爲安西將軍…荊州刺史 is a different event and predates Yin Hao’s 346 Yang post. 殷浩傳 dates 於是與溫頗相疑貳 to after 桓溫既滅蜀 (永和三年, 347). This chapter’s 時 follows Wang’s 會稽 appointment and sits with 及浩將北伐 / 果為姚襄所敗 (352–353). 345–353 is Huan Wen’s western-command career, not uncertainty about the named 不協.

evidence.quote: 時殷浩與桓溫不協，羲之以國家之安在於內外和

itemChecks.event: Yao Xiang turned on Yin Hao and routed his northern expedition.
itemChecks.reason: The dated owner is Yao Xiang’s own victory, 果為姚襄所敗, the same Shan Sang revolt named in 穆帝紀: 永和九年冬十月…使平北將軍姚襄爲前鋒，襄叛，反擊浩. Emperor Mu, 永和九年, conventionally AD 353. The claim is year-precision only; the tenth month does not require a day conversion, and in proleptic Gregorian 永和九年十月 begins 353-11-13, still AD 353. A reign-year label is not being treated as a Gregorian calendar day.

itemChecks.event: Yin Hao held Yang province and pressed a northern campaign that Yao Xiang then wrecked.
itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 351–353 repeats claim-169 and does not match Yin Hao’s supported personal events in this chapter. s0024 already attests him as 揚州刺史 before Wang’s 護軍/會稽 move; 帝紀 places that title from 永和二年 (346) to degradation in 永和十年 (354), and the defeat in 永和九年 (353). An active hint of only 351–353 drops the inspectorate attested in the owned units and should be rebuilt from the corrected events.

evidence.quote: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之

itemChecks.event: The hint lacks Shang Ziping's own dated event; Wang Xizhi only invokes his resolve.
itemChecks.reason: AD 25–57 treats a retrospective model-citation as Shang Ziping’s living activity across Guangwu’s reign. The owned Chinese has no date for Shang’s own act. Active hints may not be fed by later reception.

itemChecks.event: Ma Midi's late-Han consolation mission east of the passes.
itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 192–194 is closer to 後漢書 than claim-171’s 189–194, but it still fails: it contradicts the claim it should track, and 194 is Ma Midi’s death at Shouchun, not an activity end given in this chapter. The attested event is the 太傅慰撫 mission of 初平三年 (192).

evidence.quote: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東

itemChecks.event: Huan Wen's rift with Yin Hao during the northern-campaign years.
itemChecks.reason: AD 345–353 starts from Huan Wen’s 安西/荊州 appointment, which this chapter does not date and which is not the 不協 named in s0035. The hint must follow Huan Wen’s own supported rift/campaign-context event, not his western command as a career span.

itemChecks.event: Yao Xiang defeated Yin Hao after being used as the campaign vanguard.
itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 353 matches Yao Xiang’s own Shan Sang victory in s0037 and 永和九年冬十月 in 穆帝紀. It does not import later reception or a career-long window.

personChecks.reason: Yin Hao’s owned items (claim-169, hints-p014) agree with each other on AD 351–353 but not with the chapter or the annals. s0024 attests him as 揚州刺史 while persuading Wang to serve, before s0034; s0035–s0038 then show the later rift, the northern campaign, and the Yao Xiang defeat. 穆帝紀 dates the Yang appointment to 永和二年 (346) and the defeat to 永和九年十月 (353), with dismissal in 永和十年 (354). Owned units contain no birth, death, or age for him; the defect is the compressed 351–353 title/activity window, not a missing life-date in the sealed text.

evidence.quote: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之，勸使應命

personChecks.reason: Shang Ziping appears only in s0030 as 尚子平之志 inside Wang Xizhi’s letter. Claim-170 and hints-p015 convert that reception into a Guangwu life span (AD 25–57). There is no birth, death, age, or dated act of Shang’s own in the owned units. A later biography may attest an earlier life event, but this sentence does not; it is a model-citation and must stay retrospective.

evidence.quote: 自兒娶女嫁，便懷尚子平之志

personChecks.reason: Ma Midi’s owned claim (189–194) and hint (192–194) disagree. Both over-extend the chapter’s one event, 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東. Hou Hanshu dates that embassy to 初平三年八月 (192) and his death separately to 興平元年 (194) at Shouchun. Owned units have no birth, death, or age. The coherent chronology is the 192 mission, with 189 rejected and 194 kept out of activity unless a separate death claim is sourced elsewhere.

evidence.quote: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東

personChecks.reason: Huan Wen’s owned claim and hint both use AD 345–353, i.e. from the Jingzhou appointment through Yin Hao’s defeat. The sealed event is only 時殷浩與桓溫不協 in the Kuaiji/北伐 sequence. 345 is 永和元年荊州, before Yin Hao was 揚州刺史; 殷浩傳 dates the suspicion to after the Shu conquest. No birth, death, or age appears in the owned units. Life/activity dates must not be filled from that earlier appointment.

Yao Xiang’s owned claim and hint both date his own rout of Yin Hao to AD 353, which matches s0037 and 永和九年冬十月 in 穆帝紀. Owned units give no birth, death, or age, and this review does not add later biography. The supplied items are consistent and do not use a later commemoration as a life date.

findings.problem: Yin Hao’s 揚州刺史 attestation and active hint are dated AD 351–353, a Kuaiji/campaign slice that is not his 永和二年 (346) appointment, not the s0024 letter’s earliest date, and not his tenure through 永和十年 (354).
findings.action: Rebuild claim-169 from Yin Hao’s own events: keep 揚州刺史殷浩 as the inspectorate attested before Wang accepted 護軍, with a start no later than 永和二年/AD 346, and date the 不協/北伐/姚襄敗 cluster to 永和八–九年 (352–353). Do not keep 351–353 as the title window. Synchronize hints-p014 to those corrected personal events.

findings.problem: 尚子平之志 is Wang Xizhi’s later model-citation, converted into a Guangwu life span (AD 25–57) and an active hint.
findings.action: Preserve the mention as retrospective-reference, or as receptionType retrospective on a narrower honor/work claim, using the letter’s own context. Remove the AD 25–57 life interval and the active hint. Do not invent a 建武 birth or activity year from this chapter.

findings.problem: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東 is dated 189–194 in the claim and 192–194 in the hint. The mission is 初平三年 (192); 189 is not when he was 太傅 or envoy, and 194 is his death, not this chapter’s activity end.
findings.action: Date Ma Midi’s own embassy to conventional AD 192 (初平三年八月). Do not start at 189. Do not treat 194 as an activity endpoint here. Synchronize hints-p016 to the mission year.

findings.problem: Huan Wen’s 不協 is dated from his 永和元年 (345) Jingzhou appointment through 353, a career window that is not the event named by 時殷浩與桓溫不協.
findings.action: Date Huan Wen’s own rift to the later Hao–Wen conflict that this chapter pairs with Wang’s Kuaiji letters and Yin Hao’s 北伐 (securely 352–353 for the campaign; not before Yin Hao’s 346 Yang post). Remove 345 as the start of this claim and synchronize hints-p017.

references.reason: Primary annal for Yin Hao’s Yang appointment in 永和二年 under Emperor Mu.

references.title: 晉書/卷008 穆帝紀

references.reason: Primary annal for Huan Wen’s 永和元年 Jingzhou/安西 appointment, distinct from the later 不協.

references.title: 晉書/卷008 穆帝紀
references.quote: 冬十月，中軍將軍殷浩進次山桑，使平北將軍姚襄爲前鋒，襄叛，反擊浩，浩棄輜重，退保譙城。
references.reason: Primary annal identifying Yao Xiang’s rout of Yin Hao as 永和九年冬十月.

references.title: 晉書/卷008 穆帝紀

references.reason: Shows Yin Hao still 揚州刺史 until 永和十年二月 and that Wang Shu had been 會稽內史 before him.

references.reason: Places the Hao–Wen suspicion after the Shu conquest, not at Huan Wen’s 345 Jingzhou appointment.

references.reason: Primary annal for Wang Dao’s death in 咸康五年, the on-or-before bound for 王丞相時.

references.reason: Primary annal for Ma Midi’s 太傅 appointment and 慰撫 mission in 初平三年.

references.reason: Separates Ma Midi’s 興平元年 death from the 192 mission so 194 is not used as this chapter’s activity end.
